title.en: Estimated planetary Kp is 0.33 (quiet) at 04:00 UTC on 22 September 2026.
title.zh: 2026 年 9 月 22 日 04:00 UTC，估計行星 Kp 為 0.33（平靜）。

summary.en: Latest reliable hour-start estimated Kp is 0.33 (0P) at 04:00 UTC. The 04:00 hour is complete (60 samples through 04:59; hour-end 0.67/1M). The trailing 05:00 hour is incomplete (13 samples through 05:12) and is not used as the headline hour. Last-180 maximum is 2.00 (first at 2026-09-22 02:48 UTC; label 2Z; last-180 window from 02:13 UTC). Published-window maximum is 2.00 (02:48 UTC; label 2Z). Window start 2026-09-21 23:14 UTC (359 samples). estimated_kp remains below 5.0.
summary.zh: 最後可靠整點估計 Kp 為 0.33（0P），取樣 04:00 UTC。04:00 時段已收滿 60 筆（至 04:59，時段末 0.67／1M）。05:00 時段尚未收滿（13 筆至 05:12），不作為主卡片整點。近 180 筆最大 2.00（最先見於 2026-09-22 02:48 UTC；標籤 2Z；近 180 筆窗自 02:13 UTC 起）；公開窗最大 2.00（02:48 UTC；標籤 2Z）。窗起點 2026-09-21 23:14 UTC（359 筆）。estimated_kp 仍低於 5.0。

evidence.method: Read the public 1-minute estimated planetary K-index JSON. Use the latest published hour-start minute of a completed hour that is not a trailing incomplete placeholder (04:00 UTC). Report last-180 and full published-window maxima.
evidence.limitations: estimated_kp is a near-real-time estimate, not the final observatory Kp. The public file is a rolling ~6-hour window and older samples drop off. Hour-start 04:00 UTC is 0.33/0P; the hour stays near quiet-to-unsettled low (ends 0.67/1M at 04:59). The incomplete 05:00 hour is excluded from the headline.

title.en: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake occurred 54 km NNW of Ende, Indonesia on 22 September 2026.
title.zh: 2026 年 9 月 22 日，印尼 Ende 北北西約 54 公里發生規模 4.7 地震。

summary.en: USGS M4.5+ day feed: mb 4.7, depth about 10 km. Current day-feed maximum is mb 5.3 (us7000tj1s, 97 km S of Sarangani, Philippines).
summary.zh: USGS M4.5+ 一日饋送：mb 4.7，深度約 10 公里。一日饋送目前最大為 mb 5.3（us7000tj1s，菲律賓 Sarangani 以南約 97 公里）。

evidence.method: Added from the public USGS all-day M4.5+ GeoJSON feed when the event first appeared in the rolling 24-hour window.
evidence.limitations: Magnitudes and locations can be revised by USGS. The day feed only retains recent M4.5+ events.
